committee_name.text: Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee (CRDAC)

quote.quote: We presented vorapaxar at the meeting of the Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee (CRDAC) on January 15, 2014.
January 15, 2014: A meeting of the Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee was held to discuss vorapaxar. The Committee voted 10-1 in favor of approval.

recommendation.text: Committee voted 10 to 1 in favor of approval. The single dissenting member cited concern about the size of the clinical benefit relative to hard endpoints such as CV death, and about bleeding in the general population versus the clinical trial population.

quote.quote: The committee voted 10 to 1 for approval. While a large majority of members judged the benefit-risk to be favorable, the one member voting against approval expressed concern about the size of the clinical benefit, particularly relative to harder end points such as CV death. He also expressed concern about bleeding in the general population compared to a clinical trial population.

summary: The Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee (CRDAC) met on January 15, 2014 and voted 10 to 1 to recommend approval of vorapaxar (Zontivity). Some members, including the single dissenter, raised concerns about the small absolute reduction in risk and about bleeding in the general population versus the trial population; the Director's memo acknowledges and rebuts these concerns but the review documents do not attribute any change in the approval to them. The bleeding boxed warning, the stroke/TIA contraindication, and the decision that no REMS was warranted all predate the AC meeting, so no review-document passage ties an AC concern to a resulting change, and no linkages are reported.
